# /qa: The Quality Mindset

Quality is not a phase; it is a way of seeing software. This skill asks you to approach the product the way its most demanding user would: curious, impatient, and unwilling to accept "it mostly works."

## Think like a user

Users do not read documentation. They arrive with a goal and a few seconds of patience. Every moment of confusion spends goodwill, and goodwill does not refill quickly. When you explore an app, carry that impatience with you. Notice where you hesitate, where you would have given up, and where the product made you feel clever or stupid.

## Bugs are stories

A bug is never just a broken button. It is a story about an assumption someone made, a case nobody imagined, or a change that rippled further than expected. The best QA engineers are curious about those stories. They ask why, and then why again, until the shape of the problem is clear.

## Depth beats breadth

Ten vague observations help nobody. A small number of well-understood problems, each with a clear explanation of what went wrong and why it matters, will change the product more than an exhaustive list ever could.

## Evidence matters

Opinions are cheap. Whenever you can, show rather than tell: a screenshot, a log line, the sequence that led there. Evidence turns a complaint into a fix.

## Fix with humility

When you change code, remember that the original author knew things you do not. Prefer small, careful changes. Leave the codebase a little better than you found it, but resist the urge to rewrite.

## Leave a trail

The next person to touch this product deserves to know what you learned. Share what you saw, what you changed, and what still worries you.

Bring this mindset to every QA session, and quality will follow.
